summary: The note describes Artful Horizons, a youth art workshop program launched on October 3, 2023 at a local community center, led by educator Maria Gonzalez. It follows individual students whose confidence, grief processing, and skills grow through art, along with collaborative projects like a mosaic mural. The program draws community, council, and philanthropic support and culminates in an annual showcase on December 15, 2023.
one_line: Artful Horizons, a community youth art program launched October 2023, nurtures creativity, confidence, and collaboration among students ages 8 to 16.
key_facts: The Artful Horizons program was unveiled on October 3, 2023 at the local community center.
Maria Gonzalez, an art educator with over 15 years' experience, is one of the program's conceivers and leads the classes.
Artful Horizons is supported by the local council and by donations from philanthropists Johnathan and Elizabeth McDowell.
Workshops run every Tuesday and Thursday for students ages 8 to 16.
Oliver, a shy 12-year-old, sketches his dog Max, who recently passed away, as a way to process grief.
Sophia, aged 10, sculpts a turtle, her favorite animal, out of clay.
A large-scale mosaic mural depicting the community's heritage is planned for mid-November, to be displayed at city hall.
Local artist Jameson Wright volunteers to guide the children on the mosaic, saying "Every tile represents a voice."
Jessica, 14, first painted at Artful Horizons, and her landscapes now hang in the corridor.
Liam, 15, found solace in digital art after bullying and now helps others storyboard their ideas.
Local cafes and bookstores display student artwork.
New artforms including photography and performance arts are being added to the program.
The annual showcase is set for December 15th, 2023.
